ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jacqueline du Pré — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three months on ocrelizumab: re-baseline MRI, B-cell depletion, fatigue, vitamin D and hand function

text.paragraph: Three months on ocrelizumab: re-baseline MRI review. [S]

Ms. du Pré returns three months after her first ocrelizumab infusion, after a re-baseline MRI five days ago. The cystitis four weeks ago cleared with nitrofurantoin, and the tingling that came back with the fever went within two days of it. She has had no new symptoms. Feeling in her fingers is almost normal except after long practice, and she practices three hours a day. She has started swimming twice a week, which helps the fatigue, and rests after lunch. She played a private recital for friends last week. She takes cholecalciferol daily. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1973-07-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Vibration slightly reduced in the left fingertips only; joint position, strength, reflexes and gait normal; no Lhermitte's sign. Nine-hole peg test 19.0 seconds right, 20.5 seconds left. EDSS 1.0

Numbness, tingling and loss of position sense in the fingers of both hands for three weeks, worse on the left, with clumsiness that makes her lose her place on the fingerboard, an electric feeling down the spine on bending the neck (Lhermitte's sign), and fatigue; a similar month of tingling in the fingers 18 months ago settled on its own. A lesion of the cervical spinal cord must be found: MRI of the brain and spine with contrast booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented loss of sensation in her fingers and fatigue. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, active: a current relapse (partial cervical myelitis at C3 to C4 with sensory loss and clumsiness of the hands) after an earlier sensory episode; dissemination in space and time on MRI, with an enhancing cord lesion and an enhancing brain lesion; CSF-specific oligoclonal bands; aquaporin-4 antibody negative; meets the 1964 McDonald criteria and the 1971 revision; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented diagnosis
S — Synthetic course, imaging and laboratory detail; linked to her documented diagnosis in October 1973.
Vitamin D deficiency: 25-hydroxyvitamin D 16 ng/mL; replacement to correct the deficiency, not as a treatment for multiple sclerosis

Acute uncomplicated cystitis (Escherichia coli) seven weeks after the first ocrelizumab course, with a pseudo-relapse: two days of returning tingling in the fingers with a low fever and no new neurological deficit; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent infection; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, on ocrelizumab (G35.A). No relapse and no new or enhancing lesions on the re-baseline MRI, which becomes the reference for future scans; the June episode was a pseudo-relapse with infection, not a relapse. Hand function nearly normal (nine-hole peg 19.0 and 20.5 seconds) and EDSS 1.0. B cells are depleted (CD19 3 per microliter), as expected, and IgG is normal. The hepatitis B surface antibody check due after her two vaccine doses was missed. [S]
Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 2 today.
Ocrelizumab 600 mg in three months, with blood count, immunoglobulins, hepatitis B surface antibody and a pregnancy test beforehand.
MRI of the brain yearly from now.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 34 ng/mL after 16 weeks: corrected. [S]
Continue cholecalciferol 4000 units daily.

Acute cystitis with a pseudo-relapse (N30.00). Resolved with nitrofurantoin; no recurrence. [S]
Problem resolved.
